title: Career Roadmap: Digital Strategist
summary: Degree pathway: Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies – Data, Society & Technology

facts.Current degree: Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies (BA / B.Sc Liberal Arts & Sciences)

blocks.text: A Digital Strategist helps organisations use digital technologies, platforms, content, data, and emerging innovations to achieve business goals. The role connects technology with customer needs, market trends, organisational objectives, and measurable outcomes.

A student specialising in Data, Society & Technology can bring an interdisciplinary perspective: understanding how technology works, how people use it, how digital platforms influence society, and how data can inform decisions.
To become job-ready, students should develop practical skills in digital marketing, analytics, user experience, business strategy, content planning, and project management.
Who is this career suited for?

items.text: Students who enjoy combining technology, creativity, and business.
Students interested in digital products, online platforms, customer behaviour, and emerging technologies.
Students who like analysing trends, solving problems, and planning digital initiatives.
Students who can communicate ideas clearly and work across technical and non-technical teams.

sections.heading: What does a Digital Strategist do?

blocks.text: Digital strategy and planning
Translate organisational objectives into digital initiatives, channel strategies, priorities, and measurable goals.
Data and performance analysis
Track traffic, engagement, conversions, customer journeys, campaign performance, and return on investment.
Audience and customer research
Understand customer needs, digital behaviour, market segments, competitor positioning, and user expectations.
Digital transformation and innovation
Identify opportunities to improve digital processes, introduce useful tools, and coordinate technology-led change.
Digital Marketing Strategy
Plan search, social media, email, paid campaigns, content distribution, and audience acquisition.
Data-Driven Strategy
Use analytics, experimentation, performance dashboards, and customer insights to guide decisions.
Digital Product & Customer Experience Strategy
Improve websites, apps, onboarding, conversion journeys, and the overall digital experience.
AI & Emerging Technology Strategy
Evaluate AI, automation, and new digital tools for their usefulness, risks, costs, and business impact.
Digital Transformation & Society
Study technology adoption, digital inclusion, platform governance, privacy, and organisational change.
Recommended undergraduate pathway

A BA, BSc, or interdisciplinary Liberal Arts / Liberal Studies degree focused on Data, Society & Technology can provide a relevant foundation. The exact degree title and available modules vary by institution.

rows.text: Digital literacy, introduction to technology and society, communication, statistics, research methods
Understand digital systems and user needs
Data analysis, digital platforms, consumer behaviour, business fundamentals, media studies
Connect technology with markets and people
Digital marketing, UX research, product strategy, web analytics, technology policy
Digital transformation, AI and society, strategic management, internship, capstone project

blocks.label: Useful electives or minors
blocks.text: Business Administration, Marketing, Economics, Statistics, Computer Science, Data Science, Media and Communication, or Design.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: This interdisciplinary degree does not automatically provide the technical depth expected for every data, software, or engineering position. Choose electives and practical projects according to the digital strategy specialisation you want to pursue.
Year 1
Build the foundation

items.text: Learn how websites, apps, search engines, social platforms, and digital services work.
Develop written communication, presentation, and research skills.
Learn spreadsheet basics and introductory statistics.
Study digital audiences, online communities, and technology's social impact.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Analyse a company's digital presence and write a short improvement plan.
Year 2
Learn digital channels and data

items.text: Study SEO, content strategy, social media, email marketing, and paid advertising fundamentals.
Learn Google Analytics concepts and web-performance metrics.
Practise Excel, data visualisation, and competitor research.
Learn customer personas, journey mapping, and basic UX research.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Create a digital campaign plan with audience segments, goals, budget assumptions, and KPIs.
Year 3
Develop strategic and analytical skills

items.text: Learn Power BI or Tableau and intermediate spreadsheet analysis.
Understand conversion funnels, acquisition costs, retention, and experimentation.
Explore digital product management, AI applications, privacy, and responsible technology.
Seek internships in digital marketing, growth, product, analytics, or strategy.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Complete two practical projects and present evidence-based recommendations.
Year 4, if applicable
Build a professional portfolio

items.text: Complete a client, campus, startup, or simulated digital transformation project.
Learn to prepare strategy decks, project roadmaps, and measurement plans.
Practise presenting recommendations to non-technical stakeholders.
Apply for graduate roles and internships aligned with your chosen specialisation.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Present a portfolio showing the problem, strategy, implementation plan, KPIs, and evaluation.

rows.text: Visualising digital performance and business metrics
Keyword research, content opportunities, competitor analysis
Wireframes, journey maps, and collaboration with designers
Planning, timelines, task ownership, and delivery
Deeper analysis, automation, and larger datasets
Research assistance, ideation, analysis support, and workflow automation

blocks.text: Students should learn tools in context rather than attempting to master everything at once. For a marketing-focused role, prioritise analytics and digital channels; for product strategy, prioritise user research, product metrics, and experimentation.

Complete at least three projects that demonstrate how you turn a digital problem into a strategy. If you do not have access to a real organisation, use a student initiative, a small business with permission, or a clearly labelled simulated case study.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Digital Presence Audit
Beginner

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Audit a website's content, navigation, search visibility, mobile experience, and calls to action.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Competitor benchmarking, prioritisation, audience understanding, and a practical improvement roadmap.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A concise strategy report with recommendations ranked by impact, effort, and cost.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Digital Campaign Strategy
Beginner–Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: A campaign plan for a student initiative, nonprofit, or fictional product.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Audience segments, channel selection, content calendar, budget allocation, and measurable KPIs.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A campaign brief and dashboard template. Clearly separate projected results from actual campaign results.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Digital User Journey Improvement
Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Map how a user discovers, evaluates, signs up for, and uses a digital service.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: User research, friction-point identification, journey mapping, and prioritised UX recommendations.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A journey map, sample wireframes, and a proposed measurement plan.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: AI Adoption Strategy
Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Propose an AI-assisted workflow for a small business or university department.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Problem selection, expected benefits, cost assumptions, human oversight, privacy risks, and evaluation criteria.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A business case and phased implementation roadmap with clear success measures.

blocks.label: Portfolio standard
blocks.text: For each project, document the problem, evidence, target audience, strategic choices, KPIs, budget assumptions, risks, and evaluation approach. Do not invent performance results or present estimates as measured outcomes.
Search for internships using several related titles because entry-level roles are not always advertised as “Digital Strategist.”

rows.text: User needs, product metrics, feature prioritisation
Search visibility, content planning, audience research
Digital workflows, technology adoption, project coordination

blocks.text: Potential employers and work environments include:

blocks.label: Consulting and professional services
blocks.text: Accenture, Deloitte, EY, KPMG, and similar consulting organisations.

blocks.label: Technology and digital platforms
blocks.text: Product companies, SaaS businesses, e-commerce platforms, and technology startups.

blocks.label: Digital agencies
blocks.text: Marketing agencies, creative agencies, performance-marketing firms, and brand consultancies.

blocks.label: Corporate strategy and marketing teams
blocks.text: Retail, finance, education, healthcare, media, and consumer businesses.

blocks.label: Social-impact organisations
blocks.text: Nonprofits and public-interest organisations working on digital inclusion, public services, and technology adoption.
These are examples to investigate, not confirmed current vacancies. Review individual job descriptions for degree requirements, experience, and required skills.
Prioritise courses that help you build demonstrable skills and portfolio work.

rows.text: Channel strategy, content planning, campaign measurement
Events, conversions, user journeys, performance reporting
Keyword research, technical SEO fundamentals, content structure
Dashboard design, KPI definitions, communicating insights
Research methods, journey mapping, usability fundamentals
User problems, prioritisation, product metrics, experimentation
Scope, milestones, risk tracking, stakeholder communication
Privacy, bias, governance, responsible technology adoption

blocks.text: Potential learning sources include Google Skillshop, Microsoft Learn, HubSpot Academy, and introductory UX or product-management courses from established providers. Check current course availability, fees, and certification requirements before enrolling.

blocks.label: Recommendation
blocks.text: Complete one course in analytics, one in digital strategy or marketing, and one in UX or product fundamentals. Apply each to a portfolio project rather than collecting certificates without practical evidence.

Senior Digital Strategist / Strategy Consultant

Other possible paths include product management, growth strategy, marketing analytics, UX strategy, technology consulting, digital innovation, and digital policy. Progression depends on experience, demonstrated results, specialisation, and the structure of the organisation.

These are broad planning estimates, not verified current salary quotations or guaranteed offers. Pay varies by city, employer, sector, portfolio, experience, and whether the role is strategy-focused, analytics-focused, or primarily campaign execution.

rows.text: Stipend varies widely; some internships are unpaid
Entry-level digital strategy or digital marketing role

blocks.text: Some entry-level roles may have titles such as Digital Marketing Executive or Digital Analyst rather than Digital Strategist. Senior leadership salaries can differ substantially from these estimates, and the figures should not be treated as a promise of earnings.

By graduation, a well-prepared student should aim to have:

items.text: An interdisciplinary understanding of data, technology, society, and digital behaviour.
Practical knowledge of digital channels, analytics, and strategy development.
Experience using data to support recommendations and define measurable outcomes.
Three or more portfolio projects demonstrating research, planning, and evaluation.
An internship, live project, or simulated case study with clearly documented contributions.
Strong presentation, communication, and project coordination skills.
Awareness of responsible AI, privacy, accessibility, and ethical technology use.

blocks.text: Final recommendation
The Data, Society & Technology → Digital Strategist pathway is suitable for students who want to work at the intersection of technology, business, people, and innovation.
For the most practical entry-level route, prioritise:

Choose a specialisation early enough to build relevant experience, but remain flexible as you discover whether your strengths lie in digital marketing, data-driven strategy, product management, or digital transformation. A degree provides the foundation; a strong portfolio and the ability to explain why a strategy should work help distinguish a candidate in the job market.
